counterproofs: CLI source changed before decision capture: evaluated body and evaluated slug are written, not preloaded values
Source changed inside executor before write: explicit refusal, source preserved and no canonical file
Source changed after first authorization: exact-byte hash check refuses
Source changed during captured-byte parsing: parser uses captured bytes, final recheck refuses stale source
Source changed during canonical write: canonical output is evaluated content, changed proposal preserved and apply_error reports partial effect
Actual captured source status draft/approved/deprecated cannot bypass earlier CLI eligibility preflight
Bare score/evaluation without canonical decision cannot invoke write executor
interface: Internal apply_promotion(target, wiki_root, full_decision, *, raw_root=None, baseline_path=None). Native CLI updated; no fallback for old caller-supplied fm/body or score-only calls.
limits: No atomic filesystem compare-and-swap against concurrent writers; check/write and check/unlink race windows remain. No crash-safe atomic file replacement proven.
When proposal changes during canonical write, canonical file may already exist; apply_error states the written destination and preserved source. No rollback or transaction across files is claimed.
Decision is an in-process trusted canonical result, not an authenticated portable authorization token. No new consumer/HTTP entrypoint accepts supplied decisions.
Body and identity derive from matching source bytes; YAML and newlines retain native serialization and audit metadata are intentionally stamped, so whole-file byte equality is not claimed.
No executable complete withdrawal proof, durable acceptance, source-consumer mapping, shared corpus/DB mutation, runtime activation, CI, commit/push/merge or deployment.
